Question: What can a change in the slope of an Arrhenius plot indicate?

Options:
A. A change in the equilibrium constant of the reaction
B. A change in the pre-exponential factor of the reaction
C. A change in the reaction order
D. A shift from the chemical regime to the diffusional regime or vice versa

Thought: An Arrhenius plot is a graph of the natural logarithm of the reaction rate constant (ln(k)) versus the inverse of the temperature (1/T). The slope of an Arrhenius plot is related to the activation energy (Ea) of the reaction. A change in the slope of an Arrhenius plot typically indicates a change in the activation energy, which can occur due to a shift from one reaction mechanism to another, such as a transition between chemical control and diffusional control in a reaction. This is described in option D.
